text:
incident-bot: ALERT — Inference path p99 spike detected in us-west-2. Streaming stalls observed. SLO breach: p99=6.8s (SLO=3.0s). Streaming error rate up to 2.7%. Dash: https://grafana.internal/d/inf-path-usw2

maria: seeing the same on traces. lots of long waits in configfetch/featureflag calls — big fanout to flags DB.

kevin: paging oncall. @jess are you able to take?

jess: I'm oncall, looking. grabbing logs and traces now.

samir: quick note from runtime traces: requests are blocked on `featureflags.get(configKey)` before streaming handshake. lots of retries piling up. example trace snippet:
```
wait featureflags.get -> timeout 2s -> retry -> total wait 6.1s -> stream start delayed
```

maria: qps to flags DB spiked ~6x after a push at 02:10UTC. circuit-breakers opened and clients retried, causing thundering herd.

kevin: also seeing auth service 429s to `/token/validate` around same window. could be correlated rate-limiter policy.

jess: reproducing a single request flow: auth -> featureflag -> model selection -> streaming start. If featureflag times out it blocks token handshake and streaming init. the retry cascade is what creates tail spikes.

ops-bot: Deploy bot: automatic rollback of edge-proxy v1.14.2 initiated (dpl-9987) due to increased 5xxs.

maria: mitigation proposal: flip emergency local config cache for streaming endpoints (flag: `emergency_local_cache`) so we avoid the DB fanout. also reduce streaming client's retry policy to 1.

samir: I can flip the flag scoped to prod/us-west-2 streaming only. recommend canary first: selector `app=streaming,region=us-west-2`.

jess: doing canary now. command: `curl -X POST https://flags.internal/flip -d '{"flag":"emergency_local_cache","env":"prod","selector":"app=streaming,region=us-west-2"}'` -> 200 OK.

kevin: while canary runs, let's add a temporary auth-rate-limit exemption for streaming: rule id `rl-exempt-stream-2329` applied to path `/v1/stream/*`. minimal risk and reduces 429s.

maria: provisioning additional read-replicas for flags DB and increasing tokens for featureflag service token bucket 200->500 r/s. ETA ~3m.

paul: customer-facing note: some enterprise tenants experienced repeated reconnects on live streams; support ticket volume +3. tagging affected tenants and opening support lane.

jess: early metrics after canary: p99 in canary group down to 3.6s, overall p99 5.1s. error rate trending down.

samir: extracted logs show configfetch errors were `timeout after 2s` while client retried 3x — that produces ~6s stall on the critical path. lowering retries should cut tail considerably.

maria: pushed streaming client change: `retries=1`. also flipped `emergency_local_cache` to on for selector. configfetch RPS dropped ~80% from peak in the first roll.

kevin: added quick-fallback policy: when config or auth latency > 1s, route to fallback model `small-llm` to keep streams warm and avoid long blocking. rule: `fallback:model=small-llm,reason=short-circuit-config`.

jess: canary -> global flip done. monitoring close. oncall handoff scheduled 06:00 UTC (in ~4h). I'll stay for monitoring until handoff.

kevin: taking handoff at 06:00 UTC. checklist for next oncall: watch p95/p99, streaming stall counts, auth 429s, featureflag DB load, revoke rate-limit exemptions after 2h stable. create postmortem owner.

paul: assigning postmortem to maria + samir. include timeline, root cause, and long-term fixes: cache priming, reduce retry cascades, limit fanout per-request, add per-customer backpressure and quotas.

ops-bot: Incident created INC-2026 by jess. Severity: Sev2. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026

jess: final pre-handoff update: us-west-2 p99=2.8s, global p99=3.0s, streaming errors <0.5%. keeping exemptions for 2h after stabilization then revert. adding timeline and notes to the incident doc.

kevin: noted — will monitor and start postmortem draft. leaving a couple of TODOs in incident doc: instrument configfetch latencies by customer id, add health-check to prevent retry cascades, and implement local persistent flag cache.

jess: thanks all. handoff complete.
